figures.caption: Figure 1: Schematic of the self-balancing update starting from a uniform distribution: choose an outcome, downweight it by α, then renormalize.

Figure 2: Log-log plots of NdN as a function of the scaling factor c for (a) uniform β = [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5] and (b) non-uniform β ∝ [1.1, 0.8, 0.9, 1.2]. In both cases p(0) is the uniform distribution. Dotted lines show the expected Θ(c−1) and Θ(c−1/2) scalings in the p(0) ̸= p∗ and p(0) = p∗ regimes respectively.

Figure 3: Predictability plots for different choices of β. (left) Relationship between prediction accuracy and the scaling c of β. (right) The ratio of the gap ∆(c) := accuracy− p∗max from the uniform baseline and the first order √ c expected scaling.
Figure 4: Log-log plots of the trade-off between adversarial accuracy and the convergence rate (NdN )−1. (a) uniform β = [0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5] and (b) non-uniform β ∝ [1.1, 0.8, 0.9, 1.2].

Figure 5: Citizen’s assembly simulation results. The effect of the rescaled bias parameter β′ = cβ on the probability that the quota constraints are met and on the worst-case individual inclusion probability.
